knowledge_entries.name: Enchanting System
facts: An Enchantment Table requires 15 Bookshelves surrounding it (with one block gap on each side) to unlock maximum level 30 enchantments.
Enchanting costs Lapis Lazuli and Experience Levels; the displayed cost is the minimum level required, not the amount consumed.
Books can be enchanted on the Enchantment Table and combined on an Anvil to apply specific enchantments to gear.
A Grindstone removes all non-curse enchantments from an item and refunds some XP based on the enchantment level.
Curse of Binding prevents removal of armor from its slot except through death or breaking; Curse of Vanishing destroys the item on death — neither can be removed by a Grindstone.
Mending uses XP orbs collected while the item is in the active hand or off-hand slot to repair it; XP is used for repair before going to levels.
Silk Touch mines blocks in their original form (e.g. Stone instead of Cobblestone, Glass, Ores as blocks, Bookshelves); mutually exclusive with Fortune.
Fortune increases drop yield from mined blocks: Fortune III gives up to 4x Diamonds, 4x Emeralds, and increased Flint, Coal, and Lapis drops.
Unbreaking reduces the chance of a tool losing durability on each use; Unbreaking III effectively triples the tool's usable lifespan.

Protection enchantments (Protection, Fire Protection, Blast Protection, Projectile Protection) all reduce damage of their type; Protection is general-purpose while the others give higher reduction for their specific type.
Thorns reflects a portion of melee damage back to attackers but increases armor durability consumption.
Sweeping Edge increases the damage dealt by the sword's sweeping attack to nearby mobs; it is exclusive to swords.
Power increases bow arrow damage; Punch increases knockback; Flame ignites arrows; Infinity prevents arrow consumption (but not tipped arrows).
Lunge is a new enchantment added in 1.21.11 (Mounts of Mayhem) exclusive to the Spear's jab attack; it propels the player horizontally in the direction they are looking, at the cost of hunger points.
The Anvil uses XP levels to combine and repair enchantments; each use adds a 'Prior Work Penalty' that doubles with every use, eventually making further repairs 'Too Expensive'.
Enchantments on gear can be viewed by hovering over them in the inventory; enchanted items display a glowing purple effect.

knowledge_entries.name: The Nether
facts: A Nether Portal is built from a minimum 4x5 frame of Obsidian (inner space of 2x3 blocks) and lit with Flint and Steel or a Fire Charge.
One block of travel in the Nether equals eight blocks in the Overworld, making it extremely efficient for long-distance travel.
Nether Fortresses contain Blaze Spawners, Nether Wart growing on Soul Sand, and Wither Skeleton spawns; they are required for potion-making progression.
Blazes drop Blaze Rods when killed by a player; Blaze Rods are crafted into Blaze Powder, required for Brewing Stands and Eyes of Ender.
Wither Skeletons spawn in Nether Fortresses and have a rare chance to drop their Skull, which is needed to summon the Wither (3 Skulls required).
Bastion Remnants are piglin-occupied fortresses containing large amounts of gold loot, Pigstep Music Disc, and Netherite Upgrade Smithing Templates.
Piglins are neutral if the player wears at least one piece of Gold Armor; they attack otherwise. They can be bartered with by throwing or placing Gold Ingots near them.
Striders walk on lava and can be ridden with a Saddle; they are steered using a Warped Fungus on a Stick (analogous to a Carrot on a Stick for pigs).
Fire Resistance potions are essential for the Nether — they negate all damage from lava, fire, Blaze fireballs, and Ghast fireballs.
Ghasts are large flying mobs that fire explosive fireballs; their fireballs can be deflected back by hitting them with any projectile or even a fist while they're in the air.
Magma Cubes are like Slimes in the Nether — they split into smaller cubes when killed and deal fire damage on contact.
Zombified Piglins are neutral undead variants of Piglins; attacking one aggros the entire nearby group, making them very dangerous in numbers.
Hoglins are hostile pig-like mobs found in Crimson Forests; they deal knockback and are repelled by Warped Fungi.

The five Nether biomes are: Nether Wastes (default, red/brown), Crimson Forest (red mushroom trees, Hoglins, Piglins), Warped Forest (blue mushroom trees, safe for players), Soul Sand Valley (soul fire, skeleton/ghast spawns), and Basalt Deltas (basalt columns, Magma Cubes).
Soul Sand slows movement and is required to brew the Wither potion; Soul Soil does not slow movement but also supports Soul Fire.
Crying Obsidian can be used to craft a Respawn Anchor, which lets players set their respawn point in the Nether using Glowstone charges.
Ancient Debris — the precursor to Netherite — is blast-resistant, immune to lava/fire, and found most commonly at Y=15 in the Nether.

knowledge_entries.name: The End and Ender Dragon
facts: The End is accessed through an End Portal found inside a Stronghold; the portal has 12 frames that must be filled with Eyes of Ender to activate it.
Eyes of Ender are crafted from Blaze Powder and Ender Pearls; throwing one in the Overworld makes it fly toward the nearest Stronghold.
End Crystals atop obsidian pillars regenerate the Ender Dragon's health as long as the dragon is within range; all crystals must be destroyed before the dragon can be defeated.
Defeating the Ender Dragon for the first time awards 12,000 XP (enough to go from level 0 to 68); subsequent defeats award 500 XP.
On its first defeat, the dragon drops 1 Dragon Egg on top of the Exit Portal as a trophy — the egg does not drop again on subsequent kills.
The Ender Dragon does NOT respawn on its own; to manually respawn it, place 4 End Crystals on the four cardinal sides of the bedrock Exit Portal.
Respawning the dragon recreates the obsidian pillars and End Crystals and resets the fight, but does NOT remove the End Gateway portals already generated.
Defeating the Ender Dragon opens End Gateway portals scattered around the outer edge of the main End island; throwing an Ender Pearl into one teleports you to the outer islands.
End Cities spawn on the outer End islands and contain End Ships; End Ships house an Elytra in an Item Frame and a Brewing Stand with potions.
Elytra enables gliding flight and can be powered with Firework Rockets for sustained flight; it can be repaired with Phantom Membranes.
Shulkers are box-shaped mobs that hide in their shells; their projectiles inflict the Levitation status effect, causing the player to float upward.
Shulker Shells (dropped by Shulkers) are used to craft Shulker Boxes, which retain their inventory when broken and can be placed inside each other.
Chorus Fruit teleports the player to a random adjacent solid block when eaten; it can teleport through walls and even remove the Elytra-flying state.
The End has void below it; falling into the void is instant death with no recovery unless a Totem of Undying is held.

knowledge_entries.name: Early Game Survival Progression
facts: On a new world, the first priority is collecting Wood by punching trees, then crafting a Crafting Table from 4 Wood Planks.
A Crafting Table enables 3x3 recipes; craft a Wooden Pickaxe first to mine Stone, then a Stone Pickaxe to mine Iron Ore.
Build a shelter before the first night — even a simple dirt or wood box prevents hostile mob spawns from reaching you.
Coal is found near the surface (Y=0 to Y=96) and is essential for making Torches; Charcoal can be smelted from Wood as an alternative.
Sheep drop Wool which, combined with 3 Wood Planks, crafts a Bed; sleeping in a Bed at night skips to daytime and sets your spawn point.
Iron Ore must be smelted in a Furnace to produce Iron Ingots; Iron tools and armor are significantly better than Stone and should be obtained early.
A full set of Iron Armor reduces incoming damage substantially and should be a top early priority; it requires 24 Iron Ingots total.
Eating food restores the Hunger bar; a Hunger bar of at least 9 (out of 10) is required for natural health regeneration.
Diamond Ore generates most commonly at Y=-58 in the current ore distribution; you need an Iron Pickaxe or better to mine it.
Enchanting should begin once you have a stable food supply, 15 Bookshelves, and enough Lapis Lazuli for a full Level 30 enchantment.
A Shield (1 Iron Ingot + 6 Wood Planks) can be crafted relatively early and is highly effective at blocking melee and ranged attacks.
The priority gear upgrade path is: Stone → Iron → Diamond → Netherite for both tools and armor.

knowledge_entries.name: Brewing and Potions
facts: A Brewing Stand is crafted from 1 Blaze Rod and 3 Cobblestone; it requires Blaze Powder as fuel (each charge brews 20 batches).
Most useful potions require an Awkward Potion as a base, which is brewed from 1 Nether Wart added to a Water Bottle.
Fire Resistance Potion: Awkward Potion + Magma Cream. Negates all fire and lava damage — essential for Nether trips.
Healing Potion: Awkward Potion + Glistering Melon Slice. Instantly restores 4 HP (2 hearts); Healing II restores 8 HP.
Strength Potion: Awkward Potion + Blaze Powder. Increases melee damage by 3 (Strength I) or 6 (Strength II) per hit.
Night Vision Potion: Awkward Potion + Golden Carrot. Allows you to see in the dark as if in full daylight.
Swiftness Potion: Awkward Potion + Sugar. Increases movement speed by 20% (Swiftness I) or 40% (Swiftness II).
Invisibility Potion: Fermented Spider Eye added to a Night Vision Potion. Makes the player invisible to mobs unless the player wears armor.
Water Breathing Potion: Awkward Potion + Pufferfish. Prevents oxygen depletion underwater.
Regeneration Potion: Awkward Potion + Ghast Tear. Regenerates health over time.
Slow Falling Potion: Awkward Potion + Phantom Membrane. Causes the player to descend slowly and take no fall damage.
Gunpowder converts any standard potion into a Splash Potion (throwable, affects entities in an area).
Dragon's Breath (collected by right-clicking the Ender Dragon's breath clouds with an Empty Bottle) converts a Splash Potion into a Lingering Potion that leaves a lasting cloud.
Adding Redstone Dust to a potion extends its duration; adding Glowstone Dust increases its potency (level II) — both cannot be applied to the same potion.
Fermented Spider Eye negates or inverts the effect of a potion (e.g., turns Healing into Harming, Swiftness into Slowness).
Weakness Potion: Fermented Spider Eye + Water Bottle (does not need an Awkward base). Used with a Golden Apple to cure Zombie Villagers.

knowledge_entries.name: Redstone Basics
facts: Redstone Dust transmits a power signal up to 15 blocks before it loses strength; a Redstone Repeater restores it to full strength.
A Redstone Repeater can introduce a delay of 1 to 4 ticks per repeater; multiple repeaters can be chained to create longer delays.
A Redstone Comparator reads the contents of a container (output strength 0-15 based on fullness) or compares two signals; it can also subtract signal strength.
Pistons push a line of up to 12 blocks when activated; Sticky Pistons pull the block directly in front of them back when deactivated.
Observers detect any block state change in the block directly in front of them and emit a 1-tick pulse on the back when triggered.
Hoppers transfer items at a rate of 1 item per 8 game ticks (4 items/second); they pull from containers above and push into containers below or to the side.
Dispensers fire projectiles (arrows, fireballs), activate usable items (buckets, Flint and Steel, armor), or dispense items when given a Redstone signal.
Droppers simply drop the item as a physical entity into the world or into an adjacent container when activated.
A Redstone Torch is always ON unless the block it's attached to receives a Redstone signal, at which point it turns OFF.
A Daylight Sensor emits a Redstone signal proportional to sky light level (daytime = strong signal); right-clicking it inverts behavior to detect nighttime.
A Target Block emits a brief Redstone pulse when hit by a projectile; the strength depends on how close the projectile hit to the center.
Note Blocks play a musical note when powered; placing different blocks beneath them changes the instrument (e.g., Gold = Bell, Sand = Didgeridoo, Soul Sand = Bass).
A 2-clock can be made with 2 Redstone Repeaters set to minimum delay forming a loop; faster clocks require Redstone Torches or Observers.
An RS-NOR Latch (2 Redstone NOR gates looped together) creates a memory circuit that holds a state (set/reset) until changed.

knowledge_entries.name: Mobs and Hostile Creatures
facts: Creepers explode 3 seconds after coming within 3 blocks of a player; they are silent until the hissing begins — back away immediately. Charged Creepers (struck by lightning) deal double explosion damage.
Skeletons fire arrows and try to maintain distance; a raised Shield blocks their arrows. They burn in sunlight unless in shade or water.
Endermen are neutral unless the player looks directly at their face (a direct eye-contact check); wearing a Pumpkin on your head prevents them from aggroing.
Phantoms spawn when a player has not slept for 3 or more in-game nights; they dive-bomb from above and deal moderate damage. They burn in sunlight.
Witches throw Splash Potions of Slowness, Weakness, Poison, and Harming at players, and drink potions defensively. They are highly resistant to most potion effects.
Slimes spawn in Slime Chunks below Y=40 and in Swamp Biomes on full-moon nights; they split into smaller Slimes when killed.
Iron Golems spawn naturally in villages to protect villagers and can be crafted using 4 Iron Blocks and a Carved Pumpkin in a T-shape.
The Warden is a powerful boss mob summoned by Sculk Shriekers in the Deep Dark; it has 500 HP and deals up to 30 damage per hit, making it the strongest mob in the game.
Pillagers patrol in small groups near villages and fire Crossbows; a Bad Omen effect (obtained by killing a Pillager Captain) triggers a village Raid if the player enters a village.
Evokers summon Fangs in a line or circle pattern and spawn Vexes; they drop a Totem of Undying on death, making them high-priority targets.
Vindicators wield Iron Axes and deal very high melee damage; Johnny (named Vindicators) will attack any mob.
Drowned spawn underwater and on land during rain; they rarely hold Tridents and Nautilus Shells, both rare drops.
Guardians and Elder Guardians spawn in Ocean Monuments; Elder Guardians inflict Mining Fatigue III on nearby players, significantly slowing mining speed.
Cave Spiders are smaller than regular Spiders, can fit through 1x1 gaps, and inflict Poison on Normal/Hard difficulty.
Silverfish spawn from Infested Blocks found in Strongholds and certain mountain biomes; breaking an Infested Block summons nearby Silverfish.
The Bogged is a swamp-dwelling Skeleton variant introduced in 1.21 that shoots Arrows of Slowness and has a slower fire rate.
The Breeze is a Trial Chamber mob introduced in 1.21 that shoots Wind Charges which knock back entities and activate buttons/levers/bells; it cannot be damaged by projectiles.
The Parched is a desert Skeleton variant introduced in 1.21.11 that shoots Arrows of Weakness, does not burn in sunlight, and spawns with Camel Husks in deserts.

knowledge_entries.name: Essential Crafting Recipes
facts: Crafting Table: 4 Wood Planks in a 2x2 grid. Required for all 3x3 recipes.
Furnace: 8 Cobblestone, Cobbled Deepslate, or Blackstone arranged in a hollow 3x3 ring (empty center). Used for smelting.
Chest: 8 Wood Planks in a hollow 3x3 ring. Single Chest = 27 slots; two adjacent Chests form a Double Chest with 54 slots.
Torches: 1 Coal/Charcoal above 1 Stick in a vertical pair = 4 Torches. Soul Torches use Soul Sand/Soil instead and produce blue light.
Shield: 6 Wood Planks + 1 Iron Ingot in a 'Y' pattern (Iron Ingot at top-center, Planks fill the remaining slots). Blocks all frontal attacks.
Bucket: 3 Iron Ingots in a 'V' shape. Carries Water, Lava, Milk, Powder Snow, and most aquatic mobs.
Pickaxe: 3 material (Planks/Stone/Iron/Gold/Diamond/Netherite) across the top row, 2 Sticks down the center column. Used to mine stone and ores.
Sword: 2 material stacked vertically in the center + 1 Stick below them. Best DPS weapon for most combat situations.
Bow: 3 Sticks in a curved pattern (top-right, center-right, bottom-right) + 3 Strings filling the gaps to the left.
Crossbow: 3 Sticks across the top, 1 Iron Ingot in center, 1 String in center-left, 1 Tripwire Hook in center-right, 2 Sticks below the hook and ingot.
Compass: 4 Iron Ingots in a plus shape around 1 Redstone Dust in the center. Points to the world spawn or a Lodestone if linked.
Clock: 4 Gold Ingots in a plus shape around 1 Redstone Dust. Displays approximate time of day.
Spyglass: 1 Amethyst Shard on top, 2 Copper Ingots below it in a vertical line. Zooms view like a telescope.

Spear (1.21.11): Crafted in a diagonal pattern — same recipe shape as a Shovel but using 1 material (top-right), 1 Stick (center), 1 Stick (bottom-left). Available in Wood, Stone, Copper, Iron, Gold, Diamond, and Netherite.
Brewing Stand: 1 Blaze Rod in center-top, 3 Cobblestone across the bottom row.
Enchantment Table: 1 Book on top-center, 2 Diamonds in the middle row (left and right), 4 Obsidian across the bottom row.
Anvil: 3 Iron Blocks across the top, 1 Iron Ingot in the center, 3 Iron Ingots across the bottom (7 Ingots total + 3 Iron Blocks = 31 Iron Ingots).
Smithing Table: 2 Iron Ingots in the top-left and top-right, 4 Wood Planks filling the bottom two rows. Required for Netherite upgrades.

knowledge_entries.name: Villagers and Trading
facts: Villagers gain professions by claiming an unclaimed Workstation nearby; breaking the workstation removes the profession and resets trades.

Workstations determine professions: Composter = Farmer, Blast Furnace = Armorer, Brewing Stand = Cleric, Lectern = Librarian, Fletching Table = Fletcher, Smithing Table = Toolsmith, Grindstone = Weaponsmith, Cauldron = Leatherworker, Cartography Table = Cartographer, Loom = Shepherd, Barrel = Fisherman, Stonecutter = Mason.
Trades use Emeralds as currency; villager trade offers refresh twice per day after the villager visits their Workstation.
Each trade has a limited number of uses per session; once maxed out, it locks until the villager restocks at their Workstation.
Villagers level up from Novice to Apprentice, Journeyman, Expert, and Master by trading with the player, unlocking better trade offers.
Zombie Villagers can be cured by first applying a Splash Potion of Weakness, then feeding them a Golden Apple; the cure takes 2-5 minutes.
Curing a Zombie Villager grants a permanent significant trade discount on all their trades — stacking cures on the same villager further reduces prices.
Hero of the Village (granted by completing a Raid) reduces all active villager prices and causes villagers to occasionally toss the player gifts.
Librarians sell Enchanted Books including Mending; rerolling their lectern (breaking and replacing it) until the desired enchantment appears is a key strategy.
Fletcher Villagers accept Sticks for Emeralds at Novice level — one of the easiest early-game Emerald farms.
Farmer Villagers buy crops (Wheat, Carrots, Potatoes, Beetroot) for Emeralds and sell high-saturation food; highly useful for automating food and emerald income.
Villagers breed when they have enough food (3 Bread, 12 Carrots, 12 Potatoes, or 12 Beetroots per parent), enough unclaimed beds nearby, and have not bred recently.
A village is defined by at least 1 claimed Bed and 1 Villager; Iron Golems spawn naturally once there are enough Villagers gossiping, based on population.
Wandering Traders appear randomly with 2 Trader Llamas, offer unique trades (rare plants, materials), and despawn after 2-3 in-game days; their trades cannot be restocked.

knowledge_entries.name: Trial Chambers, Mace, and Crafter
facts: Trial Chambers are large underground structures built from Copper and Tuff blocks, introduced in Java Edition 1.21 (Tricky Trials).
Trial Spawners adjust their mob count and difficulty based on how many players are nearby, making them scale with group size.
Completing a Trial Spawner rewards Trial Keys that are used to open Vault blocks; each player can open each Vault only once per world.
Drinking an Ominous Bottle activates the Bad Omen effect, which transforms nearby Trial Spawners into Ominous Trial Spawners for harder challenges.
Ominous Trial Spawners summon armored mobs that throw status-effect potions; they reward Ominous Trial Keys upon completion.
Ominous Vaults require Ominous Trial Keys and contain the rarest Trial Chamber loot, including Heavy Cores.
The Breeze is a wind-based hostile mob exclusive to Trial Chambers; it attacks using Wind Charges and can activate buttons, levers, and bells. It is immune to projectiles.
The Mace is a powerful melee weapon crafted from 1 Heavy Core (top) and 1 Breeze Rod (below it); it deals increasing smash damage the farther you fall before hitting a target.
A successful Mace smash attack completely cancels all accumulated fall damage for the attacker at the moment of impact.
Heavy Cores are extremely rare and can only be obtained from Ominous Vaults inside Trial Chambers.
Wind Charges (dropped by Breezes) can be thrown to create small explosions that push entities and activate buttons/levers; they deal no block damage.
The Crafter is a new Redstone-powered block (added in 1.21) that auto-crafts items when given a Redstone pulse, using items stored in its 3x3 internal grid.
In the Crafter, individual slots can be 'disabled' by clicking them, allowing partial recipes and control over what is crafted.

knowledge_entries.name: Beacon System and Pyramids
facts: A Beacon is crafted from 1 Nether Star (dropped by the Wither), 3 Obsidian, and 5 Glass blocks.
To activate, a Beacon must sit on a pyramid of mineral blocks (Iron, Gold, Diamond, Emerald, or Netherite); mixed block types are allowed.

Pyramid tiers and effects: Tier 1 (3x3 base, 9 blocks): Speed or Haste. Tier 2 (5x5 + 3x3, 34 blocks): adds Resistance or Jump Boost. Tier 3 (7x7 + 5x5 + 3x3, 83 blocks): adds Strength. Tier 4 (9x9 + 7x7 + 5x5 + 3x3, 164 blocks): enables secondary effect (Regeneration) or upgrades primary to level II.
A full Tier 4 Beacon lets the player select one primary effect at Level II (e.g., Haste II) and a secondary effect of Regeneration.
Haste II from a Beacon combined with an Efficiency V Diamond or Netherite Pickaxe enables 'insta-mining' standard stone blocks.
The Beacon beam requires an unobstructed view of the sky; stained glass placed above it changes the beam's color without blocking the effect.
Beacon buffs apply within a cylindrical radius: Tier 1 = 20 blocks, Tier 2 = 30, Tier 3 = 40, Tier 4 = 50 blocks; the buff extends from bedrock to sky.
Players must feed the Beacon an Iron Ingot, Gold Ingot, Diamond, Emerald, or Netherite Ingot to select or change the active effect.
Beacon effects last 9 seconds after leaving the radius (with a brief grace period extension) before expiring.

knowledge_entries.name: Farming and Food
facts: Crops (Wheat, Carrots, Potatoes, Beetroots) require tilled Farmland; Farmland is created by right-clicking Dirt or Grass with a Hoe.
Farmland within 4 horizontal blocks of a water source becomes hydrated (darker brown color) and grows crops significantly faster than dry farmland.
Crops grow via random ticks; growth speed is increased by light, hydration, and nearby crops of the same type not immediately adjacent (farmland bonus).
Bonemeal can be applied directly to crops to instantly advance their growth by one stage; multiple applications are usually required to fully grow a crop.
Wheat Seeds come from breaking tall grass; Carrot, Potato, and Beetroot are found in Village farms, shipwreck supply chests, and dungeon loot.

Food values: Cooked Steak (8 hunger, 12.8 saturation), Cooked Porkchop (8 hunger, 12.8 saturation), Golden Carrot (6 hunger, 14.4 saturation — highest saturation in game), Bread (5 hunger, 6 saturation).

Animal Breeding: feed two of the same passive animal their preferred food to trigger breeding (5-minute cooldown per parent): Cow/Mooshroom/Sheep = Wheat, Pig = Carrot/Potato/Beetroot, Chicken = any Seeds, Rabbit = Dandelion/Golden Carrot/Carrot.
Cows drop Raw Beef and Leather; Sheep drop Raw Mutton and Wool (shearing with Shears produces 1-3 Wool without killing the sheep).
A Composter converts plant-based items (crops, flowers, saplings, etc.) into Bone Meal over 7 fill stages; different items have varying composting success chances.
Sugarcane grows 1 block per 18 random ticks adjacent to Water and is used to craft Paper (for Maps and Books) and Sugar.
Melons and Pumpkins grow from stems on hydrated farmland; the fruit spawns on an adjacent grass, dirt, or farmland block next to the mature stem.
Nether Wart grows on Soul Sand in the Nether (or anywhere in a Nether Fortress area); it does not require water or light and has 4 growth stages.
Suspicious Stew can be crafted with a Mushroom, Bowl, Flower, and Wheat to create a soup with a hidden status effect based on the flower used.
Cake requires 3 Milk Buckets, 2 Sugar, 1 Egg, and 3 Wheat; it is placed as a block and can be eaten in 7 bites, each restoring 2 hunger.
Glow Berries grow in Lush Caves on Cave Vines hanging from the ceiling; they emit light (level 14) and restore 2 hunger when eaten.

knowledge_entries.name: Netherite Upgrade Progression
facts: Ancient Debris spawns in the Nether and is most concentrated at Y=15; it is blast-resistant and completely immune to fire and lava.
Ancient Debris must be mined with at least a Diamond Pickaxe; it is typically found in veins of 1-3 and never exposed to air naturally.
Smelting Ancient Debris in a Furnace or Blast Furnace produces Netherite Scrap; combining 4 Netherite Scrap + 4 Gold Ingots in a crafting grid yields 1 Netherite Ingot.
To upgrade Diamond gear to Netherite, use a Smithing Table with a Netherite Upgrade Smithing Template + the Diamond item + 1 Netherite Ingot.
Netherite Upgrade Smithing Templates are found in Bastion Remnant chests; they can be duplicated using 7 Netherrack + 1 Diamond + the template.
Netherite gear retains all enchantments from its Diamond base when upgraded via the Smithing Table.
Netherite armor and tools have higher durability, faster mining/attack speed, and more enchantability than Diamond.
Netherite items float in lava and do not burn, making them recoverable if dropped in lava.
Netherite Horse Armor (added in 1.21.11) can be obtained by upgrading Diamond Horse Armor using a Smithing Table and a Netherite Upgrade template.

knowledge_entries.name: Cave Exploration and Mining
facts: Below Y=0, stone transitions to Deepslate; Deepslate ore variants take roughly 1.5x longer to mine but drop the same materials as their stone counterparts.
Diamond Ore is most common at Y=-58 to Y=-59 and requires at least an Iron Pickaxe to mine; strip-mining at Y=-57 (one block above bedrock layer range) is highly effective.
Iron Ore generates in two peaks: common near the surface (Y=15-56) and in large blobs deep underground (Y=-24 and below); it is smelted into Iron Ingots.
Gold Ore generates most between Y=-16 and Y=32 in the Overworld; in the Nether, Gold Ore generates between Y=10 and Y=117 and can be mined with Fortune for extra nuggets.
Lapis Lazuli Ore has its peak at Y=0 and is required for Enchanting; Silk Touch is not needed since Lapis drops directly.
Redstone Ore peaks at Y=-59 and drops 4-5 Redstone Dust (more with Fortune); it also glows when touched.
Copper Ore peaks at Y=48 and is used to craft Spyglasses, Lightning Rods, and decorative Copper blocks; Copper oxidizes over time but can be waxed with Honeycomb.
Emerald Ore only generates in Mountain biomes and peaks at Y=236 near high mountain peaks; it is the rarest ore in the Overworld.
Lava pools generate frequently below Y=10 and in large caverns; always carry a Water Bucket to convert lava to Obsidian or Cobblestone and create a barrier.
The Deep Dark biome generates below Y=-51 and contains Sculk blocks, Ancient Cities, and the Warden.
Ancient Cities are enormous Deep Dark structures containing chests with Enchanted Books, Swift Sneak Leggings (unique enchantment), Echo Shards, and Disc Fragments.
Sculk Sensors detect vibrations (footsteps, block placement, projectiles) within 8 blocks and emit a Redstone signal; sneaking completely suppresses vibration detection.
Sculk Shriekers produce warning wails when activated; if a player triggers them 4 times while darkness is active, the Warden is summoned.
Dripstone Caves contain stalactites and stalagmites of Pointed Dripstone; stalactites drip water or lava into Cauldrons below and deal fall damage when they collapse.
Lush Caves (located below Azalea trees on the surface) contain Glow Berries, Spore Blossoms, Moss blocks, and Axolotls in underground water pools.
Mineshafts generate underground and contain rail tracks, Minecart Chests with loot, and Cave Spider Spawners surrounded by Cobwebs.

knowledge_entries.name: The Wither Boss
facts: The Wither is summoned by placing 4 blocks of Soul Sand or Soul Soil in a T-shape (one on top, three in a row) and placing 3 Wither Skeleton Skulls on the top 3 spots.
The Wither cannot be summoned in the End dimension; it is typically spawned in the Nether or a contained area in the Overworld.
On summoning, the Wither creates a large explosion; always build a containment structure and trigger it from a distance.
The Wither has 300 HP (150 hearts) on Normal and 600 HP on Hard; it can pass through all blocks except Bedrock and End Portal Frames.
The Wither shoots black Wither Skulls that inflict the Wither effect (deals 1 damage per second, can kill), and a charged blue Wither Skull that destroys blocks.
When the Wither drops below 50% HP, it gains a shield that blocks ranged attacks; melee or Smite-enchanted weapons are required to deal damage.
Defeating the Wither drops a Nether Star, the required ingredient to craft a Beacon.
Wither Roses are dropped by any mob killed by the Wither; they inflict the Wither effect on any entity that touches them.
Beheading enchantment (from an Ominous Vault) causes mobs to drop their head when killed; otherwise skulls are only obtained rarely.
A Wither can be trapped in Bedrock or a Bedrock-ceiling area to be unable to flee, making the fight easier; this technique is valid in vanilla survival.

knowledge_entries.name: Combat and Armor
facts: Swords have higher DPS than axes due to their faster attack speed and can use Sweeping Edge to hit multiple mobs; axes deal more single-hit damage and can disable shields for 5 seconds.
A raised Shield (right-click and hold) blocks all frontal melee and projectile damage; axes and Evoker Fangs can bypass or disable shields.
Critical hits are triggered by attacking while falling (not sprinting or on the ground); they deal 150% base damage and display star particles.
Bows must be fully charged (hold right-click until the bow shakes) for maximum 9 damage output; Charge arrows arc over distance.
Crossbows can be pre-loaded and held ready to fire instantly; they can load Firework Rockets for area damage. The Multishot enchantment fires 3 arrows at once.
Armor's total reduction: Leather = 7 points, Gold = 11, Chain = 12, Iron = 15, Diamond = 20, Netherite = 20 (plus Toughness). Each armor point reduces damage by ~4%.
Armor Toughness (Diamond = 8 total, Netherite = 12 total across a full set) reduces the percentage of damage that bypasses armor from powerful hits.
The Trident can be thrown for a ranged attack and recalled with Loyalty; Riptide propels the player forward in rain or water when thrown; Channeling summons lightning during thunderstorms.
The Mace deals escalating fall-damage bonus strikes: each block of fall before hitting adds extra damage; a large fall can one-shot most mobs.

The Spear (added in 1.21.11) has two attacks: a quick Jab (low damage, knockback, multi-hit) and a Charge attack (high damage scales with player/target speed, can dismount riders); it has a longer reach than any other melee weapon but requires minimum distance.
Totem of Undying (held in either hand) prevents death once: the player is saved at 1 HP, gains Absorption II, Regeneration II, and Fire Resistance II for a few seconds.
Fire Aspect sets a target on fire; Flame does the same for bows. Looting III significantly increases rare drops (e.g., Wither Skeleton Skull chances increase from ~2.5% to ~5.5%).
Smite (up to V) and Bane of Arthropods (up to V) are enchantments that deal bonus damage against Undead and Arthropod mobs respectively; they are mutually exclusive with Sharpness.
Aqua Affinity helmet enchantment removes the mining speed penalty underwater; Depth Strider boots increase movement speed while submerged.

knowledge_entries.name: Storage and Transportation
facts: A single Chest holds 27 slots; two adjacent Chests merge into a Double Chest with 54 slots. Trapped Chests emit a Redstone signal when opened.
Ender Chests have 27 personal slots that are shared across all Ender Chests for that player; contents are not lost on death. Breaking one requires Silk Touch.
Shulker Boxes hold 27 items and retain their inventory when broken; they can be placed inside other storage (except other Shulker Boxes).
Hoppers transfer 1 item every 8 game ticks (2.5 items/second); they pull from containers above and push into containers below or beside them.
Powered Rails accelerate Minecarts when powered by Redstone; a repeating powered rail circuit can maintain speed. Detector Rails emit a Redstone signal when a cart passes.
Boats are the fastest overland water travel and can fit 2 entities; they do not break at high speed unless hitting a solid block head-on.
Horses require repeated mounting (without a Saddle) until hearts appear to tame; a Saddle and optionally Diamond/Netherite Horse Armor is then equipped.
Donkeys and Mules can carry a Chest (15 extra slots) when right-clicked with one; Mules are bred from a Horse and Donkey.
Camels can seat 2 players simultaneously and their tall height prevents most melee mob hits; they can dash forward at the cost of a cooldown.

Nautilus (added in 1.21.11) is a tameable aquatic mount found in ocean biomes; tamed with Pufferfish, equipped with a Saddle, and grants Breath of the Nautilus effect (pauses oxygen depletion) while riding.
Striders walk on lava in the Nether and can be saddled and controlled with a Warped Fungus on a Stick.
Llamas can be equipped with a Carpet (cosmetic) and Chest (3-15 slots depending on strength); leading one with a Lead causes others nearby to form a caravan.
An Item Sorter automates storage using Hoppers, Comparators, and single filtered items in Hoppers to direct items into specific chests by type.
Elytra (found in End City Ships) enables gliding flight; right-clicking a Firework Rocket while gliding provides a speed boost.

knowledge_entries.name: World Generation and Biomes
facts: The Overworld is divided into biomes that each have distinct terrain, climate, mob spawns, and resources.
Plains biomes are flat and common; they naturally spawn Villages and are easy for early building and farming.
Desert biomes contain Desert Temples, Villages, and Fossils; no water spawns naturally on the surface, and Husks replace Zombies.
Jungle biomes contain Jungle Temples, Bamboo, Cocoa Beans, Parrots, and Ocelots; they are dense and difficult to navigate.
Ocean biomes come in Warm (coral reefs, tropical fish), Lukewarm, Normal, Cold, and Frozen variants; Ocean Monuments spawn in all Deep Ocean types.
Mountain biomes include Jagged Peaks, Frozen Peaks, Stony Peaks, Snowy Slopes, Meadow, and Grove variants; Emerald Ore and Goats are exclusive to mountains.
Swamp biomes contain Slime spawns at night, Blue Orchids, and Witch Huts; Mangrove Swamps (a variant) feature Mangrove trees and Mud.
Badlands (Mesa) biomes contain exposed Gold Ore in their cliffs, Mineshafts at the surface, and rare Cactus + Red Sand terrain.
The Cherry Grove is a pink cherry blossom biome with Cherry Log trees that drop Cherry Petals; it has pastel pink fog and is peaceful.
Taiga biomes have Spruce trees, Foxes, and Wolves; Snowy Taiga adds cold temperatures and Rabbits.
The Savanna biome is flat with Acacia Trees; Villages and Llamas spawn here.
Lush Caves are underground biomes found below Azalea trees on the surface; they contain glow berries, Spore Blossoms, Moss, and Axolotls.
Dripstone Caves are rocky underground biomes filled with Pointed Dripstone stalactites and stalagmites.
The Deep Dark biome is found deep underground (below Y=-51) and always contains Sculk; Ancient Cities sometimes generate in very large Deep Dark areas.
Villages generate in Plains, Desert, Savanna, Taiga, and Snowy Plains biomes; each has a distinct architectural style.
Ruined Portals generate in both the Overworld and Nether as partially destroyed Nether Portal frames with Magma Blocks and Gilded Blackstone nearby.

knowledge_entries.name: Structures and Loot
facts: Dungeons are small rooms with a Monster Spawner (Zombie, Skeleton, or Spider) and 1-2 Chests containing Iron Ingots, Buckets, Saddles, Enchanted Books, Music Discs, and more.
Strongholds are massive underground fortresses containing the End Portal; located by following Eyes of Ender. Chests contain Ender Pearls, Iron items, and Enchanted Books.
Ocean Monuments are giant Prismarine structures found in Deep Ocean biomes; protected by Guardians and Elder Guardians (who inflict Mining Fatigue III). Contain Gold Blocks inside.
Woodland Mansions are rare large structures in Dark Oak forests containing Vindicators, Evokers (who drop Totems of Undying), and Vex; loot includes Enchanted Books and rare items.
Desert Temples have a central chamber with 4 Chests and a pressure plate TNT trap; loot includes Diamonds, Emeralds, Enchanted Books, and Gold Ingots.
Jungle Temples contain 2 Chests accessed by solving a lever puzzle or a tripwire trap; loot is similar to Desert Temples.
Shipwrecks generate in oceans and beaches; Supply chests contain food, Map chests contain Buried Treasure Maps, and Treasure chests contain Emeralds and Diamonds.
Buried Treasure is found by following Treasure Maps (from Shipwreck/Ocean Ruins); it contains a Heart of the Sea, Diamonds, and high-value loot. It is always under an X on the map.
Pillager Outposts are watchtower structures containing Pillager spawners; they often have a cage with a Golem, a Witch, or other mobs below.
Bastion Remnants come in 4 types (Bridge, Hoglin Stables, Housing Units, Treasure Room); the Treasure Room contains the highest-value Netherite and gold loot including Netherite Upgrade Templates.
End Cities generate on the outer End islands and always spawn in clusters; End Ships (which spawn adjacent to some End Cities) are the only source of Elytra.
Trial Chambers are underground copper/tuff structures containing Trial Spawners, Vaults, and Ominous Vaults with unique loot including Heavy Cores and Mace-related items.
Ancient Cities are massive Deep Dark structures containing chests with Swift Sneak (unique enchantment), Disc Fragments for the 'otherside' disc, Echo Shards for Lodestones, and Enchanted Books.
Igloos in Snowy Plains biomes sometimes have a basement with a Zombie Villager in a cage and a Splash Potion of Weakness + Golden Apple — hinting at how to cure Zombie Villagers.
Ocean Ruins (Warm = sandstone, Cold = stone) contain loot chests with archaeology Suspicious blocks nearby; breaking Suspicious Sand/Gravel with a Brush reveals buried items including Pottery Sherds.

knowledge_entries.name: Mounts of Mayhem (1.21.11 Features)
facts: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.11, named 'Mounts of Mayhem', was released on December 9, 2025 and is the final version to use the classic 1.x.y version format.
The Nautilus is a new neutral aquatic mob that spawns in all ocean biomes; it can be tamed using Pufferfish, equipped with a Saddle, and ridden underwater.
Riding a tamed Nautilus grants the Breath of the Nautilus effect, which pauses the player's oxygen depletion (but does not replenish it).
The Zombie Nautilus is an undead underwater mob that always spawns with a Drowned rider wielding a Trident; it burns in sunlight unless equipped with Nautilus Armor.
Nautilus Armor comes in Copper, Iron, Gold, Diamond, and Netherite variants; it is worn by Nautilus mobs and found in Buried Treasure, Ocean Ruins, and Shipwreck chests.
The Camel Husk is an undead Camel variant that spawns in Deserts at light level 0 with a Husk (holding a Spear) in front and a Parched in the back; it doesn't burn in sunlight.
The Parched is a desert Skeleton variant that shoots Arrows of Weakness, doesn't burn in sunlight, and is immune to the Weakness effect; it spawns in Deserts replacing some regular Skeletons.
Zombie Horses can now be tamed in survival, healed using Red Mushrooms, equipped with a Saddle and Horse Armor, and ridden like a regular Horse; defeating their Zombie rider yields the mount.
Netherite Horse Armor is obtained by upgrading Diamond Horse Armor at a Smithing Table using a Netherite Upgrade Smithing Template and a Netherite Ingot.
The Spear is a new tiered melee weapon (Wood, Stone, Copper, Iron, Gold, Diamond, Netherite) crafted in a diagonal pattern similar to a Shovel but diagonal.
The Spear has two attacks: Jab (quick, low damage, hits multiple enemies, triggers Lunge enchantment) and Charge (hold to build up, damage scales with player/target velocity, can dismount riders).
The Spear has extended reach compared to all other melee weapons but requires a minimum distance from the target to deal damage.
The Lunge enchantment (Spear exclusive, levels I-III) propels the player horizontally during a Jab; higher levels increase distance but cost more hunger (I=0.5, II=1, III=1.5 hunger points).
Zombies, Husks, Zombified Piglins, and Piglins can spawn holding Spears; Piglins prefer Gold Spears.
Tamed Horses no longer path into Cacti or Sweet Berry bushes (quality-of-life improvement in 1.21.11).

knowledge_entries.name: Dimensions and Portals
facts: Minecraft has three main dimensions: the Overworld (base survival world), the Nether (hellscape), and the End (endgame dimension).
Nether Portals link the two dimensions at an 8:1 ratio — 1 block in the Nether = 8 blocks in the Overworld for horizontal travel.
End Portals are one-way from the Overworld to the End; to return, players must die or use the Exit Portal (opened after defeating the Ender Dragon).
The Respawn Anchor (crafted from 6 Crying Obsidian + 3 Glowstone) lets players set a respawn point in the Nether; it holds up to 4 charges (filled with Glowstone).
Using a normal Bed in the Nether or End causes it to explode violently; use a Respawn Anchor in the Nether and accept death in the End.
The Overworld's Y range is from Y=-64 (bedrock floor) to Y=320 (build limit); Y=0 is sea level, and Y=64 is the standard surface height.
Lodestones (crafted from 1 Netherite Ingot + 8 Chiseled Stone Bricks) can be linked to a Compass anywhere in any dimension, including the Nether and End.
The void in the End starts below Y=0; falling into it is instantly fatal and cannot be countered by a Totem of Undying.
Chorus Fruit (from the outer End islands) teleports the player to a random adjacent solid block surface and can clip through walls; it also cancels Elytra flight.

knowledge_entries.name: Core Game Mechanics
facts: The day-night cycle lasts 20 real-world minutes (24,000 game ticks); daytime is 10 minutes, sunset/sunrise are 90 seconds each, and nighttime is approximately 7 minutes.
Hostile mobs spawn in light levels of 0 only (since 1.18); torches, lanterns, and glowstone prevent mob spawns in enclosed areas.
The Hunger bar has 20 points (10 drumsticks); natural health regeneration requires 18+ hunger points and costs hunger. Below 6 hunger, the player cannot sprint.
Experience (XP) is gained from killing mobs, smelting, breeding, mining, fishing, and trading. XP is used for enchanting and Anvil repairs.
Death drops all items on the ground at the location of death; items despawn after 5 real minutes. Death Coordinates are shown in the respawn screen.
Sleeping in a Bed sets your respawn point to that Bed; if the Bed is blocked or destroyed, you respawn at the world spawn instead.
Game ticks run at 20 per second (50ms each); Redstone, mob AI, and crop growth all operate on the tick system. Random ticks trigger crop growth, fire spread, and ice melting.
The Moon phase (full moon to no moon, 8 phases over 8 in-game days) affects Slime spawning — more Slimes spawn during a Full Moon.
Lightning strikes can strike during thunderstorms and convert Pigs to Zombified Piglins, Creepers to Charged Creepers, Villagers to Witches, and Horses to Skeleton Horses.
Difficulty levels: Peaceful (no hostile mobs, no hunger drain), Easy (mobs deal less damage), Normal (standard), Hard (mobs deal more damage, Zombies break doors, starvation can kill).
In Hard difficulty, Zombies can break down wooden doors during sieges; Iron Doors (opened by Redstone only) are immune to this.
The inventory has 36 general slots (27 main + 9 hotbar), 4 armor slots, 1 off-hand slot, and a 2x2 personal crafting grid.

knowledge_entries.name: Ocean and Aquatic Gameplay
facts: The Trident is only obtainable by killing Drowned mobs that spawn holding one; it cannot be crafted.

Trident enchantments: Loyalty (returns to player after throwing), Riptide (propels player forward in water/rain), Channeling (summons lightning during thunderstorms — only one of Riptide or Channeling, and only Loyalty or Riptide, can coexist).
Ocean Monuments are guarded by Guardians (laser beam attack) and 3 Elder Guardians (Mining Fatigue III curse); the interior contains 8 Gold Blocks in the central chamber.

A Conduit is crafted from 1 Heart of the Sea + 8 Nautilus Shells; when activated inside a 3-layer Prismarine frame structure, it grants Conduit Power (unlimited water breathing, night vision, and haste) to nearby players.
Dolphins grant a temporary speed boost to nearby players who sprint-swim close to them; they are attracted to items dropped in water.
Sea Turtles lay Eggs on beaches that hatch into Baby Sea Turtles; killing a baby drops a Scute (5 Scutes = 1 Turtle Shell helmet, which grants Water Breathing).
Axolotls spawn in dark underground water near clay blocks (Lush Caves); they can be scooped into a Bucket and deployed to fight Guardians and Drowned.
Coral blocks and Coral Fans only survive underwater (they dry out and die without water); Silk Touch mines them intact.
The Heart of the Sea is found only in Buried Treasure chests (one per chest); it is required to craft a Conduit.
Kelp grows underwater and can be smelted into Dried Kelp (portable food) or used to craft Dried Kelp Blocks (efficient fuel = 200 seconds burn time).
